title: OpenAI is finally merging ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs
content:
The ChatGPT desktop app can be a confusing piece of software, given that there are ChatGPT and Codex sections, and within the former, there are Chat and Work tabs. With so many options, it’s sometimes easy to forget where you are working and where exactly your project is.
In an apparent effort to address this, OpenAI is now gearing up to merge the Chat and Work tabs within the ChatGPT experience, according to an email sent to users. OpenAI said that initially, this experience will be available to select users for feedback before it is rolled out widely.
“This will enable you to move from exploring an idea to having ChatGPT carry it through, all in one place. You can bring in your files and plugins and ask ChatGPT to build a website, create a presentation, or do things for you on the web, while reviewing and guiding its work. Codex will remain a separate experience in the ChatGPT desktop app,” the email said.
OpenAI also said with this transition, both ChatGPT and Codex will draw tokens from the same allowance pool. It said this change won’t impact most users, but based on usage and model, some folks might need to wait for resets more frequently.
Rival Anthropic merged Claude’s chat and Cowork functions into one screen in September.

report.summary: OpenAI will merge ChatGPT's Chat and Work tabs into a unified workspace, first testing with select users while keeping Codex separate and pooling token allowances.
report.background: ChatGPT's desktop app has grown into a multi-surface product: a ChatGPT section with Chat and Work tabs, plus a separate Codex area. That structure made it easy for users to lose track of where a project lives and which mode they are using. OpenAI's move reflects a broader shift in the AI assistant market from simple chat interfaces toward agentic workspaces where users bring files, plugins, and instructions and let the assistant execute multi-step tasks. Anthropic merged Claude's chat and Cowork functions into one screen in September, signaling that rivals see reduced interface friction as a competitive advantage. OpenAI is testing the merged experience with select users before a wider rollout, and it is also aligning token accounting across ChatGPT and Codex.
key_points: OpenAI is merging the Chat and Work tabs inside ChatGPT into a single experience, initially for select users to gather feedback before a broad rollout. Codex will remain a separate section in the desktop app, preserving a dedicated coding environment.

The unified workspace is meant to support an idea-to-execution flow: users can bring files and plugins, ask ChatGPT to build a website, create a presentation, or perform web tasks, and review and guide the work in one place.
ChatGPT and Codex will draw from the same token allowance pool. OpenAI says most users will not be affected, but depending on usage and model choice, some may need to wait for resets more frequently.

The change follows Anthropic's September merger of Claude's chat and Cowork functions into one screen, highlighting a race among AI assistant makers to simplify interfaces and support longer, agentic workflows.
report.impact: The merge signals that leading AI assistants are converging on a unified workspace model: chat is becoming the entry point, not the whole product. For the industry, differentiation will depend less on conversational quality and more on execution, file handling, plugins, and how smoothly users can supervise multi-step work. For developers, the shared token pool makes usage planning more important, especially for teams mixing ChatGPT and Codex; heavy coding or advanced-model use may hit limits faster. Regular users should see less confusion and fewer context switches, but they may also notice quota pressure if they rely on both chat and coding features. The overall direction is toward assistants that act more like operable workbenches than standalone chat windows.
report.tools: Watch the ChatGPT desktop app for the merged workspace, Codex for coding, and Anthropic's Claude/Cowork for a competing unified design. To approximate similar workflows, try Open WebUI or LibreChat for self-hosted multi-model chat with files and tools; AnythingLLM for document-centric workspaces; and Aider, Cline, or Roo Code for coding agents. These open-source options offer pieces of the unified workspace experience, though not OpenAI's exact integration or token model.
